stories.headline: Claude Sonnet 5's Launch Discount Expires, Raising API Prices 50% Overnight
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic let Claude Sonnet 5's $2/$10 launch pricing expire on schedule, raising API rates 50% to $3/$15 per million tokens just as the company pursues a roughly $2 trillion valuation.

pull_quote.text: We handed Claude Sonnet 5 a two-part job — update Salesforce account tiers, send a launch announcement to enterprise contacts — and it finished end to end. That used to stall halfway.

data_points.label: Per million input tokens, up from $2
Per million output tokens, up from $10

stories.article_excerpt: Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5, the mid-tier model the company built to make AI agents cheap enough for everyday automation, just got 50% more expensive.

stories.headline: South Korea's Wrtn Raises $72M as AI Entertainment App Hits $7.2M Monthly Revenue
stories.key_takeaway: Wrtn Technologies raised a $72M Series C at a $722M-plus valuation, powered by its OOC entertainment app hitting $7.2M in monthly revenue within three months of launch.

pull_quote.text: For the past five years since our founding, we have established ourselves as Korea's leading AI service company and demonstrated our global competitiveness, which enabled us to successfully complete this funding round.

stories.article_excerpt: South Korean AI company Wrtn Technologies has closed a Series C funding round of roughly 100 billion won, betting that consumer AI entertainment scales as fast as enterprise tooling.

stories.headline: The Average Company Now Runs 13 AI Agents, Up From Five a Year Ago
stories.key_takeaway: Salesforce's Agentic Enterprise Index shows committed Agentforce adopters tripled their agent counts and skill sets in a year, though the sample reflects only businesses already deep into the platform.

pull_quote.text: These agents are expanding beyond their initial scope to really become cross-functional.
pull_quote.role: Head of Agentic Commerce Insights, Salesforce

data_points.label: Average agents per org, up from 5
Average skills per agent, up from 2

stories.article_excerpt: The average company running Salesforce's Agentforce platform now operates 13 distinct AI agents, up from five in early 2025 — with one large caveat about who was counted.

stories.headline: A $19.4B AI Data Center in New Jersey Faces Complaints Over 62 Unpermitted Gas Turbines
stories.key_takeaway: Residents and watchdogs allege the Microsoft-linked DataOne data center in Vineland, New Jersey is running unpermitted gas turbines, turning AI's power demand into a local fight over permits, noise and emissions.

pull_quote.text: It's just constant. It never goes away.
pull_quote.role: Vineland resident living near the DataOne site

stories.article_excerpt: A $19.4 billion Microsoft-linked AI data center rising on a former baseball field in Vineland, New Jersey has become a test of whether permitting law can keep pace with AI's appetite for power.

stories.headline: French Startup Uncovr Raises €6M to Turn Surgical Video Into Billing-Ready Records
stories.key_takeaway: Uncovr raised €6M led by Index Ventures to turn surgical video into automated operative reports and billing codes, betting operating-room footage is healthcare's next underused data asset.

pull_quote.text: Surgeons should not have to spend their time reconstructing from memory what a camera has already captured and becoming medical coders.

data_points.label: Clinical detail typically omitted from op reports
Cases with missing billable steps found

stories.article_excerpt: Paris-based startup Uncovr has raised roughly €6 million in seed funding led by Index Ventures to attack one of medicine's most stubborn time sinks: the paperwork after the operation.

stories.headline: OpenAI's GPT-Live Ditches the Text Pipeline — But Its Sub-300ms Claim Doesn't Hold Up
stories.key_takeaway: GPT-Live's full-duplex architecture eliminates ChatGPT Voice's old speech-to-text-to-speech pipeline and cuts response-time jitter fivefold, but independent testing found a 205ms median latency edge rather than the breakthrough some coverage implied.

pull_quote.text: GPT-Live (next-generation voice) launches today in ChatGPT. It feels magical and 'real'. I have always preferred typing to talking to an AI, now I think that's going to shift.

data_points.label: Measured latency edge over Advanced Voice Mode

stories.article_excerpt: OpenAI's marquee bet on natural voice conversation has now had nearly two months in the wild, and the picture independent testing paints is more nuanced than the launch messaging.

stories.headline: OpenAI Retires the Standalone DALL-E GPT, Closing a Chapter in Generative Imagery
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI retired the branded DALL-E GPT inside ChatGPT on August 30, pushing users to the general ChatGPT Images feature, days after also pulling o3 from the model picker.

pull_quote.text: On August 30, 2026, we're retiring the official DALL·E GPT in ChatGPT. We encourage you to download any images you want to keep before then.

stories.article_excerpt: OpenAI quietly closed the book on one of generative AI's founding products this weekend, folding a five-year-old brand into the chat window that replaced it.

stories.headline: Grok Crosses From Recommending to Buying — If the Screenshot Holds Up
stories.key_takeaway: A viral claim that Grok autonomously completed a Tesla Model Y purchase remains unverified beyond social media, but it lands squarely in the gap that agent-payment standards like Google's AP2 and the proposed AI AGENT Act are racing to close.

pull_quote.text: A right to revoke means very little until the enterprise can answer what is being revoked, from whom, and across which systems.

data_points.label: Grok first added to Tesla vehicles

stories.article_excerpt: A screenshot posted to X showed something the agentic-commerce industry has mostly only demoed: an AI agent taking an order all the way to checkout. Verifying it is another matter.

stories.headline: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 Flash Caps a 16-Model August as Open Weights Close the Gap
stories.key_takeaway: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 Flash closed out a record 16-model August with vendor-reported benchmark wins, underscoring how narrow the gap between open-weight and proprietary frontier models has become.

pull_quote.text: It plays the same role that Qwen3-Next played for Qwen3.5 — the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention design introduced at that time has since been used across the Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Qwen3.7 and Qwen3.8 series.

data_points.label: Fastest tracked output speed, Ling 3.0 Flash

stories.article_excerpt: Alibaba's Qwen team closed out August by shipping Qwen3.8 Flash, an open-weight model that undercuts proprietary rivals on price while trading blows with them on vendor-run benchmarks.

stories.headline: A New Software Category Emerges: Tools That Audit the AI Agents Writing Your Code
stories.key_takeaway: As AI coding agents gain autonomy, a new category of independent audit tools is emerging to inspect agent-written code for security holes, hallucinated packages and leaked secrets before it reaches production.

pull_quote.text: We're not building another tool meant to replace the developer. We want to give companies the ability to use agents whose capabilities are already enormous, but in an environment where the organization retains control over the data, the process and accountability for the final decision.

data_points.label: Severity of a 2026 coding-agent CLI flaw
Secrets found exposed in public MCP configs

stories.article_excerpt: As AI coding agents graduate from autocomplete tool to unsupervised committer, a new category of software is emerging — one that does not write code, but watches what the agents write.

stories.headline: 'Prefix Sliding' Makes Long-Reasoning Models 3x Faster by Forgetting Their Own Work
stories.key_takeaway: Prefix Sliding keeps only a model's original instructions plus a window of recent reasoning tokens, capping inference cost at a constant rate for a reported 3x speedup with no retraining — though coding tasks need much larger windows.

pull_quote.text: We find most intermediate reasoning tokens lose importance as the model continues reasoning. This calls into question whether retaining them is worth the cost.

data_points.label: Window needed to match full attention on code

stories.article_excerpt: A reasoning model that thinks for an hour drags a growing anchor behind it. A new preprint asks whether it needs to carry that weight at all.

stories.headline: Anthropic Says Automated Researchers Can Make Other Models Safer With Little Human Input
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic reports its automated researchers closed the safety gap on all ten tested alignment failures and beat human researchers on deception, while flagging real limits on how far the approach generalizes.

pull_quote.text: The best AAR method beats what experienced humans propose, on average within six hours. Human guided research directions do not lead to stronger performance.

data_points.label: Deception gap closed, automated vs human
Hourly cost, automated vs human researcher

stories.article_excerpt: Anthropic says it has automated a chunk of its own alignment research process — a result that is either encouraging or unsettling depending on which part of the field you sit in.

stories.headline: South Korea Will Give All 52 Million Residents a Free National AI Assistant
stories.key_takeaway: South Korea selected SK Telecom, KT and Kakao consortia to build a free, domestic-model-powered national AI chatbot for all 52 million residents, with a beta in September and full rollout by year end.

pull_quote.text: AI for All is more than just a service; it is the calculator and computer of the AI era.
pull_quote.role: Minister of Science and ICT, South Korea

stories.article_excerpt: South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT confirmed which companies will build a government-funded AI assistant for every resident — a test of AI as public utility.

stories.headline: X Removes 200,000 China-Linked Accounts It Says Pushed Anti-Data-Center Messaging
stories.key_takeaway: X says it removed a 200,000-account network with roughly 200 accounts pushing anti-data-center narratives, but an independent researcher found many of those posts had no followers or engagement at all.

pull_quote.text: No real humans saw these posts about data centers.

stories.article_excerpt: X says it dismantled a network of roughly 200,000 accounts it links to China. Independent analysis suggests almost nobody saw the posts that made the story newsworthy.

stories.headline: Revised FRONTIER Act Picks Up Backing as Congress Circles Frontier-Model Rules
stories.key_takeaway: Public Knowledge's endorsement of the revised FRONTIER Act, after opposing its predecessor over broad preemption, signals a narrower compromise that could give federal frontier-AI rules real momentum against an 85-law state patchwork.

pull_quote.text: That one-to-one preemption, where any law preempted is replaced with an adequate federal framework, is exactly what Public Knowledge has called for in the past.

data_points.label: Compute threshold for a covered model

stories.article_excerpt: Public Knowledge, one of the loudest critics of Congress's first attempt at a federal AI safety framework, has endorsed the second — and the reason why is the preemption fine print.

stories.headline: New Benchmark Finds Top Video Models Solve Barely Half of Visual Reasoning Tasks
stories.key_takeaway: VGI-Bench finds the best video-generation model solves only 51% of process-sensitive visual reasoning tasks, and models almost never correct their own mistakes mid-generation.

pull_quote.text: The solution state does change during denoising, but almost never toward a correct one.
pull_quote.role: VGI-Bench preprint, UIUC / Tsinghua / MIT / Microsoft Research

data_points.label: Tasks and instances in the benchmark

stories.article_excerpt: A new benchmark finds even the best commercial video-generation models solve barely half of a set of visual reasoning tasks — and rarely notice when they are wrong.

stories.headline: Australia Launches a 'Buy Australian AI' Push to Get Domestic Models Into Enterprises
stories.key_takeaway: Canberra's Buy Australian AI Partnership uses bank-led matchmaking and an accelerator rather than procurement mandates to get local AI startups in front of enterprise buyers, starting with financial services.

pull_quote.text: If we fail to build a strong AI industry around our own data and ingenuity, we will be a more vulnerable, and less prosperous country.
pull_quote.role: Assistant Minister for Science, Technology and the Digital Economy

stories.article_excerpt: Australia's federal government has thrown its weight behind a scheme designed to get local AI companies into enterprise procurement pipelines — without mandating that anyone buy them.

stories.headline: At TechBBQ, Europe's AI Conversation Kept Circling Back to Who Controls the Stack
stories.key_takeaway: Europe's AI sovereignty debate has moved from models to the full stack — compute, foundation models and now network capacity — with real money attached but no consensus on whether duplicating the US stack is worth the cost.

pull_quote.text: I am embarrassed today at the level of quality of our network.

data_points.label: Public investment behind EU AI gigafactories
Mistral debt financing for EU data centers

stories.article_excerpt: At TechBBQ in Copenhagen, the question underneath every AI panel was not which models Europe can build, but who owns the infrastructure those models run on.
